newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end higher on Ramos' assurance.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end higher on Ramos' assurance.

text.p: * Main index up 1.11 percent to 3,338.67 points
Manila stocks jumped at the close on Monday on bullish sentiment after President Fidel Ramos gave an assurance that he is not seeking re-election after his term expires in 1998, dealers said.
"If the President pursues what he says it will be good for the market," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities. The main index ended at its day's peak of 3,338.67 points, up 36.69.
Ramos' assurance and the Philippine credit upgrade "raised the level of comfort of investors," he added.

Local brokerages have been worried that a political row over the ruling party's efforts to secure a second term for Ramos could affect the business climate. The Philippine constitution restricts a president to a single six-year term.

Louie Bate, analyst at ING Barings, said investors bought blue chips that have lagged behind the market like Petron SM Prime, and Ayala Land towards the end of the session. "Bargain hunting during the last minutes of session gave a kick to a slow start," he said.
"I think we may see some money moving back into blue chips for the rest of the week," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Equities. Speculative issues dominated trading last week.
